findings.declaration: CuntzTrace.Positive.rootExponent (and its downstream uses, e.g. ExtendedTrace.apply_le_rank, rank_eq_iSup_cuts, rank_eq_iSup_cuts_all)
findings.problem: rootExponent is a bare def with no simp-normal-form lemmas. Every use that needs its value or limit has to unfold the definition inside simp. That happens in this file at `simpa [Positive.rootExponent] using h` (apply_le_rank) and at three `simpa [Positive.rootExponent] using (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat : ...)` calls (rank_eq_iSup_cuts, root_scalars_tendsto_one, rank_eq_iSup_cuts_all). The same pattern appears in about 15 other files in Pureness and JiangSu. Unfolding exposes the raw `1 / (↑n + 1)` form in ℝ≥0, so the outcome depends on how simp then normalises casts and `one_div`. The tendsto fact is restated with an explicit type ascription each time.
findings.proposed_change: Add a small interface next to the definition. First, `@[simp] lemma rootExponent_zero : rootExponent 0 = 1`, which would let apply_le_rank use `power_one` through simp without unfolding the definition. Second, a lemma `rootExponent_coe (n) : (rootExponent n : ℝ) = 1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1)` (or `= ((n:ℝ)+1)⁻¹`), proved once by `simp [rootExponent]`. Third, one `tendsto_rootExponent : Tendsto (fun n => (rootExponent n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0)` and `Tendsto rootExponent atTop (𝓝 0)` in ℝ≥0, derived from `tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat`. The four unfold-and-simpa sites here, and the other copies, would then become `exact`/`simpa using tendsto_rootExponent`.
findings.benefit: Simp has a stable, definition-independent normal form for the root exponents. The repeated type-ascribed `simpa [rootExponent] using (tendsto_one_div_add... : ...)` blocks go away in this file and in the other call sites. If rootExponent's definition changes, only the interface lemmas need to be reproved.

findings.excerpt:
lemma rank_normalize (τ : ExtendedTrace A) (a : Positive A) :
    τ.rank (Positive.normalize a) = τ.rank a :=
findings.problem: rank_normalize is an unconditional equation. Its right-hand side is strictly simpler than its left-hand side, so it is a natural simp lemma and cannot cycle. It is not tagged @[simp], so every user has to name it explicitly. In this file it is passed by hand to `simp only [one_mul, τ.rank_normalize] at ht` and `simpa only [τ.rank_normalize] using hr n`. It is also used through `rw` or `← rank_normalize` in RankBounds.lean and RankFunctorial.lean. Any plain `simp` call on a goal containing `τ.rank (normalize a)` leaves the normalisation in place.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp] lemma rank_normalize ...`. Its direction is already the right one for simp, and it is unconditional, so no discharger is needed. Keep `rank_smul` without @[simp], since it needs the side condition `0 < s`.
findings.benefit: Rank goals that mention normalised elements reduce to the rank of the original element under plain `simp`. Several `simp only [τ.rank_normalize]` and `rw [τ.rank_normalize, ...]` call sites can be simplified. The unconditional scale-invariance fact becomes part of the default simp set for rank.

evidence.declaration: rank bound proof using rank_normalize by rw
